gen_21 was not this edit: it cut line-initial "Maybe" (2.68 → 1.71 per 1k tokens) but raised lowercase "maybe" (0.54 → 0.84). A boosted 22.387 would suppress the whole family, lowercase included (z 20.3). So the built-in Maybe brake has never been tested. The rates also show the doubt impulse being re-routed under C: the original writes Wait 24.3 times and line-initial Maybe 0.46 times per 1k tokens, while C writes Wait 0.07 and Maybe 2.68 times. That is a 6-fold rise in exactly the token that 22.387 brakes, and these Maybe lines carry the interpretation-doubt spirals I saw in the GSM loops. X6 (C + 22.387 output column ×2) is now saved. I will test it on SH512 (S1 + H1, 512 answers), where C's answers with the same seeds already exist (gen_13 and gen_16_edited), giving a paired comparison with SE about 2 points. X6 was found from weights and older activation data, not by selecting on these outcomes. Confirmation: higher accuracy than C with fewer Maybe lines and fewer cut answers. Refutation: no accuracy change (doubt simply re-routed again, as with gen_21) or more wrong answers. I will first try passing the ID file directly; a failed request costs no pass.
